text: Nor are we to use living creatures like old shoes or dishes, and throw them away when they are worn out or broken with service; but if it were for nothing else, but by way of study and practice in humanity, a man ought always to prehabituate himself in these things to be of a kind and sweet disposition.
author: Plutarch
translation: John Dryden et al., rev. Arthur Hugh Clough, 1864
